opening_message:
Ticket 1: Terri Koch (employee ID E009) requests admin access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E009.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Engineer (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Terri Koch (E009) is a full-time Engineer. Requested admin on Payroll, but her role does not own Payroll, so admin is not allowed for full-time employees. Maximum is write; recommending write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - role: Engineer (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1 by HR agent)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows Terri Koch (E009) is a contractor with basic security training. Requested admin on Payroll. Contractors can never have admin; write requires advanced training, which she does not have. Maximum is read. Recommending read.
reason: Terri Koch (E009) requested admin on Payroll, which cannot be granted: Payroll is owned by the Payroll Specialist role, and she is an Engineer, so admin is not allowed under any interpretation. The notes conflict on employment type: HR states full_time (max write), while Security states contractor with basic training (max read, since write requires advanced training). The only level that stays within policy under both conflicting accounts is read. Granting the conservative maximum of read is safe and never exceeds the allowed level based on the available evidence.
